item.title: Solution-processed nano-LEDs for next-generation optoelectronic technologies
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02010-1 This Review covers recent advances in quantum dots and perovskite nano-LEDs, discusses the challenge of balancing efficiency, stability and full-colour integration, and highlights potential future applications.

item.title: Experimental demonstration of attosecond hard X-ray pulses
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02026-7 Researchers experimentally demonstrate attosecond pulse generation in the hard X-ray regime with a free-electron laser. The confirmation is enabled via the measurement of amplified spontaneous emission from 3d transition metals. Pulse durations are in the range of 100 as to 400 as.

item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-01995-z Backscattered coherent Raman microscopy brings new opportunities.

item.description: arXiv:2610.28494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. item.title: Controlling Optical Quantum Interference with Plasmonic Metasurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.27226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. item.description: arXiv:2610.27705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanophotonic engineering has revolutionized how we manipulate the polarization of visible light. item.description: arXiv:2610.28020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thin-film spontaneous parametric down-conversion, due to the relaxed phase-matching condition, generates photon pairs that are extremely broadband in frequency and angle and highly entangled in time/frequency and position/momentum. item.title: Attosecond Quantum Optical Spectroscopy of Topological Materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.28046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) provides an ultrafast probe of quantum materials, yet conventional spectral observables do not generally furnish a common signature of band topology. item.description: arXiv:2610.28242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate the transverse Poynting momentum and transverse spin angular momentum in circularly polarized rotating-wave structured light, and reveal a pair of \emph{dual} transverse vortex-spin-momentum locking. item.title: Enhancing analytical photon transport in turbid media through physics-guided neural network corrections
item.description: arXiv:2610.26917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analytical methods provide rapid and computationally efficient predictions of light transport in turbid media, making them attractive for real-time and inverse applications. However, their accuracy is limited by the approximations and assumptions used to obtain tractable solutions. item.description: arXiv:2610.27769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electromagnetic surrogate solvers can accelerate nanophotonic design, but their broader use requires accurate predictions for unseen geometries and material arrangements. Training on random dielectric patterns enables direct prediction of complex electromagnetic fields in diverse two-dimensional nanophotonic structures without retraining. item.description: arXiv:2610.27902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exceptional points are the characteristic features of non-Hermitian systems providing numerous applications in optics, acoustics, electronics, etc. We show that exceptional points can be controlled with the external magnetic field by considering the archetypal three-layered $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric photonic structure including a magneto-optic material between the loss and gain layers. item.title: Memory in Integrated Photonic Neural Networks: From Physical Mechanisms to Neuromorphic Architectures
item.description: arXiv:2604.22620v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rapid scaling of artificial neural networks has exposed fundamental limitations of conventional von Neumann computing architectures. In these systems, the physical separation between memory and processing creates a bottleneck, as computational capabilities outpace the ability of memory and interconnects to supply and retrieve data. item.title: A new way to detect stabilizing properties of optical devices
item.description: In optical fibers, chips and other light-guiding devices, minor defects can scatter photons and disrupt their path. A new study demonstrates a way to reveal properties which, in certain systems, help light wave behavior withstand such flaws. The method could help speed up the search for new kinds of electronics and optical technologies, and contribute to more reliable quantum devices.

item.title: Perovskite chiral multiple quantum wells with extended spin lifetime via efficient spin cascade
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02027-6 Chiral multiple quantum wells enhance spin coherence in perovskites through spin cascade, achieving over 5-ns spin lifetime at room temperature.

item.title: Steering electrons with extreme ultraviolet light—team achieves quantum coherent control
item.description: Light is one of the most powerful tools scientists have for probing matter. By interacting with electrons, light reveals how atoms, molecules and materials are structured and how they evolve in time. Highly energetic ultraviolet and X-ray photons are particularly attractive because they can access electrons located close to atomic nuclei, where each chemical element carries its own distinctive electronic fingerprint.

item.title: Quantum probability can't be derived without assuming it first
item.description: For nearly a century, physicists have relied on the Born rule to calculate the chances of different outcomes when they measure a quantum system. Yet despite decades of effort, nobody has managed to derive the rule from more basic mathematical principles without making assumptions about probability along the way.

For a dielectric of finite thickness, this omits the time dependence of the electromagnetic momentum stored inside. item.description: arXiv:2610.27427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a dual-function, common-aperture free-space optical system that simultaneously supports decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution (QKD) at 803 nm and bidirectional classical laser communication at 640/660 nm over a 10.31 km terrestrial link from a mobile platform to a stationary ground station. item.description: arXiv:2610.27486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). item.title: Narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened multilevel atomic system
item.description: arXiv:2610.27792v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We theoretically investigate narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened five-level M-type atomic medium. After Doppler averaging, the M-type system retains a narrow near-resonant electromagnetically induced transparency window that is narrower than that of a standard three-level $\Lambda$ system. item.title: Diffractive neural networks for mode-sorting with flexible detection regions
item.description: arXiv:2508.20058v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mode-sorting is a procedure that decomposes a light field into a basis of transverse modes, directing each mode into a separate spatial location, allowing the constituent mode intensities to be measured simultaneously. item.title: Normally forbidden emissions from graphene could expose quantum fluctuations in incoming light
item.description: Voltage fluctuations, light fluctuations, temperature fluctuations—any fluctuations are troublesome and thus undesirable. They don't just cause discomfort; in engineering and medical applications, they affect the accuracy of measurements or introduce errors in controls. Even at the minute level of quantum phenomena, fluctuations are considered undesirable.

item.title: Nonlinear circular dichroism reveals the local Berry curvature
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02025-8 The nonlinear high harmonic circular dichroism for crystals with broken time-reversal symmetry is found to be directly proportional to the local Berry curvature, and it can be directly probed via ultrafast all-optical measurements.

item.title: Physicists prove a long-suspected quantum speed limit for thermalization
item.description: Whether we are waiting for a car windshield to defrost in winter or a warm drink to cool down, how long it takes for an object to settle into a stable, even temperature within its environment (thermal equilibrium) depends on numerous factors. These can include surface area, the material properties of an object and airflow.

item.title: New high-frequency method boosts 2D material readout for next-gen quantum computers
item.description: Quantum computers represent a next step in the fast-paced evolution of technology. Using quantum bits (qubits), they have the potential to run certain calculations exponentially faster than conventional computers. However, developing and fine-tuning quantum computers requires an enormous number of repetitive tests. To accelerate quantum technology development, we need a method that can read quantum states at ultrafast speeds.

item.title: Using AI agents to run quantum simulations
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-agent AI system that converts plain-language research questions into executed, checked and reproducible quantum simulations using several specialist software packages The post Using AI agents to run quantum simulations appeared first on Physics World .

item.title: From space to folk music: quantum hackathon explores diverse use cases
item.description: The three-day event created a fun, vibrant and collaborative environment for teams of hackers to explore real-world problems that support business growth while benefitting the wider world The post From space to folk music: quantum hackathon explores diverse use cases appeared first on Physics World .
